name: Nasi Goreng
pitches: The default answer for a reason: smoky, filling, and somehow always right.
When you can't decide, the wok decides for you.
Fried rice with a fried egg on top. You already know this is a good idea.

name: Mie Ayam
pitches: Springy noodles, sweet-savoury chicken, broth on the side. Cheap comfort done right.
Add sambal, add pangsit, add happiness.
The between-classes classic. Fast, warm, never disappointing.

name: Bakso
pitches: Hot broth, bouncy meatballs. Rainy-day energy in a bowl.
A little kecap, a lot of sambal, and the day gets better.
Some days just need soup. Today sounds like one of them.

name: Soto Ayam
pitches: Turmeric broth, shredded chicken, a squeeze of lime. Gentle and bright.
Light enough for a morning, warm enough for a whole afternoon.
The bowl that fixes a long day without slowing you down.

name: Ayam Geprek
pitches: Crispy chicken, smashed into sambal. Pick your level and be brave.
The student budget hero: crunchy, spicy, and very filling.
If you want heat, this is the honest answer.

name: Nasi Padang
pitches: Rendang, gulai, sambal ijo. A whole feast on one plate.
Big appetite? Padang has never once left anyone hungry.
Point at what you want. That's the whole menu experience.

name: Sate Ayam
pitches: Charcoal smoke and peanut sauce. Your nose already said yes.
Skewers taste better after dark. That's just science.
Sweet, smoky, and great for sharing (or not sharing).

name: Gado-Gado
pitches: Vegetables that actually taste exciting, thanks to that peanut sauce.
Light, fresh, and still satisfying. The smart pick.
Eat your greens without it feeling like a sacrifice.

name: Pecel Lele
pitches: Crispy fried catfish, raw sambal, warm rice. Tenda food at its best.
The tent-stall dinner Depok runs on.
Crunchy, spicy, cheap. Hard to argue with that.

name: Martabak Manis
pitches: Thick, buttery, loaded with chocolate and cheese. Bring friends. Or don't.
Dessert that counts as dinner if you believe hard enough.
Late night plus martabak equals a good decision.

name: Seblak
pitches: Chewy krupuk in a fiery kencur broth. Choose your toppings, choose your pain.
For when you want your mouth to feel something.
Customisable chaos in a bowl. In a good way.

name: Indomie Telur
pitches: It's 1 a.m. and the warmindo is open. You know what to do.
The national midnight snack, made better by someone else's stove.
Cheap, fast, and exactly what a deadline night needs.

name: Nasi Uduk
pitches: Coconut rice, fried chicken, sambal kacang. A proper start to anything.
Fragrant rice that makes every side dish better.
Breakfast of champions, Betawi edition.

name: Bubur Ayam
pitches: Soft, warm, and easy on a sleepy stomach.
Stirred or not stirred? Either way, a gentle morning win.
The breakfast that feels like being looked after.

name: Siomay Bandung
pitches: Steamed fish dumplings drowned in peanut sauce. Snack or meal, your call.
Light enough to keep going, tasty enough to want more.
The cart outside campus knows what you need.

name: Pempek
pitches: Chewy fish cakes with sweet-sour cuko. Tangy in the best way.
Kapal selam with a whole egg inside. Go big.
When you want something different from rice and noodles.

name: Dimsum
pitches: Little steamed baskets of joy. Order more than you think.
Shareable, snackable, and great when you can't commit to one thing.
Hakau, siomay, bakpao: variety on one table.

name: Ramen
pitches: Rich broth, chashu, a jammy egg. Worth the little splurge.
Treat yourself. You've had a week.
Deep, slow-cooked flavour for a not-so-slow price.

name: Rice Bowl
pitches: Chicken teriyaki or sambal matah, all in one tidy bowl.
Easy to eat between classes, easy to like.
Everything you need, nothing you don't.

name: Burger
pitches: Smashed patty, melted cheese, toasted bun. Sometimes simple wins.
Two hands, no regrets.
A craving this specific deserves to be answered.

name: Tteokbokki
pitches: Chewy rice cakes in sweet-spicy gochujang. Drama-watching food.
Sweet first, spicy second, addictive third.
Add cheese. Trust the process.

name: Ayam Bakar
pitches: Kecap-glazed, charred at the edges, smoky all the way through.
The grill does the convincing. You just eat.
A proper meal for a proper hunger.
